surfaces.part: cracked concrete slab patches and dirt ground, seen from above as a flat ground overlay

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile seen from above: dirt texture with concrete slab patches. The only vertical-looking features are 1px dark lips under south breaks and thin seam lines, which are outlines and not a front face of 3 or more rows. The column scan shows alternating dirt and concrete runs with no top band, front-edge line, eave shadow or ellipse. For a flat decal this is the correct reading: no front face, so top_down_slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 5 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references. The concrete ramp has roughly 4 steps (highlight rim, light, mid, dark lip), against about 6 for the Beodeul paving. The dirt reads as 3 browns in clustered blotches with clod shapes. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the lips and rims are tinted dark grey-blue or brown rather than a black sticker line. The concrete carries speckle grain, seam lines and cracks, and the broken edges are ragged with loose chunks. Only 12 colours in total keeps it a little leaner than the references, but it has no flat fills and no uniform black outline. A careful artist would accept it beside the references.
